sections.content: How many people are "further education teaching professionals"?

42,855 people

were counted on the census as "further education teaching professionals" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Further education teaching professionals supervise and teach trade, technical, commercial, adult education, secondary and post-secondary courses to students beyond minimum school leaving age.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "further education teaching professionals", 14.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "further education teaching professionals" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "further education teaching professionals" included:

  • residential, day and domiciliary care managers and proprietors
  • crane drivers
  • managers in transport and distribution

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More women than men had this job

Among people working as "further education teaching professionals" there were more women than men (56.5% compared with 43.5%).

This means "further education teaching professionals" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "teaching and other educational professionals".

Men made up 43.5% and women made up 56.5% of "further education teaching professionals"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "further education teaching professionals" included:

  • catering and bar managers
  • financial accounts managers
  • newspaper, periodical and broadcast editors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "further education teaching professionals" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "further education teaching professionals" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "further education teaching professionals", 12.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (64.6% compared with 35.4%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.5%) than self-employed (6.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
